;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Syrian civil war]], [[Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)]], [[Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War]]
**[[Syrian Army]] shelling kills [[Turkish Armed Forces|Turkish military]] personnel in [[Idlib Governorate]], prompting retaliation by Turkish forces. A pro-opposition war monitor says the Turkish retaliation killed 13 Syrian soldiers, which Syria denies. The [[Ministry of Defence (Russia)|Russian Ministry of Defence]] says [[Turkey]] moved troops "inside the de-escalation zone [...] without notifying the [[Russian military intervention in the Syrian Civil War|Russian side]]". [[President of Turkey|Turkish President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan|Erdoğan]] says the Syrian shelling killed five Turkish soldiers and three civilian personnel, with nine others injured, and that the Russians "need to stand aside". [https://apnews.com/3d67f5af98809d06e47600ea3568c8be (AP News)] [https://sana.sy/en/?p=184182 (SANA)] [https://www.npr.org/2020/02/03/802221255/turkey-syria-trade-deadly-strikes-as-russia-watches-uneasily (NPR)]
*A [[National Gendarmerie|gendarme]] is stabbed and wounded in [[Metz]], [[Grand Est]], [[France]], by a [[French Army|soldier]] who shouted [[Islamic extremist]] slogans and declared that he is an [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|Islamic State]] member. He was shot and wounded. [https://www.lefigaro.fr/actualite-france/attaque-de-la-gendarmerie-de-dieuze-le-parquet-de-metz-n-exclut-pas-un-acte-terroriste-20200203 (''Le Figaro'')]
*Gunmen open fire in an [[amusement arcade]] in [[Uruapan]], [[Mexico]], killing at least nine people, including three children. Police say the gunmen were searching for specific targets but then opened fire indiscriminately on customers. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/feb/04/video-arcade-attack-mexico-michoacan (''The Guardian'')]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**The global [[Cruise Lines International Association]] bans trips to [[mainland China]] and says that it "will deny boarding to any individual, whether guest or crew, who has travelled from or through mainland [[China]] within the previous 14 days". [https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/world/2020/02/03/Cruise-ships-to-ban-recent-China-visitors-Global-industry-body.html (Al Arabiya English)]
**[[Thailand]] announces the possible discovery of a "cure" for the [[SARS-CoV-2|coronavirus]] after a confirmed coronavirus patient tested negative for the virus 48 hours after being given an "anti-HIV" drug. [https://filipinotimes.net/news/2020/02/03/thai-cures-novel-coronavirus-patient-cocktail-hiv-flu-drugs/ (''Filipino Times'')] [https://www.dailysabah.com/health/2020/02/02/thailand-cures-coronavirus-with-anti-hiv-drug-cocktail-in-48-hours (''Daily Sabah'')] [https://www.ibtimes.sg/thailand-may-have-found-cure-wuhan-coronavirus-hiv-influenza-drug-cocktail-cures-chinese-womam-38757 (''IB Times'')] 
**[[Huoshenshan Hospital]], opening after ten days of construction, admits the first patients of the pandemic. [https://yp.scmp.com/news/china/article/115508/coronavirus-outbreak-built-10-days-chinas-virus-hospital-takes-first (''SCMP'')] [https://apnews.com/8e978ecbb3b1dd125221b627d35e8edc (AP)]
*[[HIV/AIDS research]]
**The United States [[National Institutes of Health]] stops its trial of an experimental [[HIV]] vaccine ([[HIV vaccine#Phase III|HVTN 702]]) amidst poor results. The trial involved more than 5,000 people in [[South Africa]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/health-51361955 (BBC News)]

;International relations
*[[Brexit|Post-Brexit]], [[United Kingdom–European Union relations]]
**[[European Union]] [[Continuing United Kingdom relationship with the European Union|negotiator]] [[Michel Barnier]] says a future trade deal is possible only if the [[United Kingdom]] "abides by EU standards". [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|British Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]] says the UK would not be bound by EU rules in any post-[[Brexit]] agreement. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/e-u-u-k-set-out-conflicting-red-lines-post-n1128536 (NBC News)]
*[[Israel–Uganda relations]]
**[[President of Uganda|Ugandan President]] [[Yoweri Museveni]] says he is "studying" the possibility of opening an embassy in [[Jerusalem]] as [[Prime Minister of Israel|Israeli Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] promises to open an embassy in Uganda if such a move takes place. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-israel-uganda/israeli-pm-hopes-uganda-will-open-embassy-in-jerusalem-in-near-future-idUSKBN1ZX1Y6?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[European migrant crisis]]
**[[Greek police]] on the island of [[Lesbos]] fire [[tear gas]] to disperse migrants and refugees protesting  about conditions in the camps and the slow pace of processing [[right of asylum|asylum]] requests. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-europe-migrants-greece-lesbos/greek-police-fire-teargas-at-protesting-migrants-refugees-on-lesbos-idUSKBN1ZX1QW (Reuters)]

;Law and crime

**A [[mass shooting]] on a [[Greyhound Lines|Greyhound bus]] headed from [[Los Angeles]] to [[San Francisco]] leaves one dead and five wounded; the motive remains unknown. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/greyhound-bus-shooting-grapevine-california-today-2020-02-03-live-updates/ (CBS News)] [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/six-wounded-california-greyhound-bus-shooting-suspect-custody-n1128581 (NBC News)]
**A shooting at a dormitory at [[Texas A&M University–Commerce]], leaves two dead and one wounded. [https://www.politico.com/news/2020/02/03/2-dead-in-shooting-at-university-residence-hall-in-texas-110547 (''Politico'')] [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/2-dead-shooting-incident-texas-m-commerce-residence-hall-n1129021 (NBC News)]

;Politics and elections
*Aftermath of the [[2019 Malawian general election]]
**The Constitutional Court of [[Malawi]] annuls the result of the country's last general election due to various irregularities. [[2020 Malawian general election|New elections]] are being scheduled to be held within 150 days. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/02/malawi-top-court-annuls-presidential-election-results-200203060112731.html?utm_source=website&utm_medium=article_page&utm_campaign=read_more_links (Aljazeera)] 
*[[2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries]], [[2020 Republican Party presidential primaries]]	
**The first nominating contest in the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] and [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]] primaries takes place in the U.S. state of [[Iowa]]. Eleven Democratic Party candidates [[2020 Iowa Democratic presidential caucuses|will challenge]] for 49 delegates, while incumbent [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]] will [[2020 Iowa Republican presidential caucuses|face two Republican challengers]] for 40 delegates, regarding the [[2020 United States presidential election]] [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-51302248 (BBC News)]
** Significant irregularities in the Democratic Party process are reported with an app being blamed for widespread confusion and delayed results. [https://www.vox.com/recode/2020/2/3/21117038/2020-iowa-caucuses-app-results (''Vox'')] [https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/opinion/angry-sanders-supporters-storm-out-of-caucus-calling-it-a-joke-and-waste-of-time (''The Washington Examiner'')]
*[[First impeachment trial of Donald Trump|Impeachment trial of Donald Trump]]
**Closing statements are delivered before the [[United States Senate]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/live/2020/trump-impeachment-trial-vote-02-03?smid=tw-nytimes&smtyp=cur#the-trial-resumes-but-with-little-of-the-intensity-and-drama-that-gripped-the-capitol-last-week (''The New York Times'')]
**Democratic Senator [[Joe Manchin]] asks his colleagues to consider [[Censure in the United States|censuring]] Trump, as an alternative to [[impeachment]], for his efforts to pressure [[Ukraine]] to investigate domestic political rivals. Senator Manchin is considered friendly with the White House. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/sen-manchin-calls-for-censuring-trump-over-pressuring-ukraine-to-investigate-his-domestic-political-rival/2020/02/03/c29a42aa-46c9-11ea-ab15-b5df3261b710_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
